surfaces.part: lake-edge terrain tile (dark teal water fill with a green grass strip on the left columns)

answer.evidence: The tile is a full 16x16 opaque block (width 16 on every row, one uniform run of rows 0-15 in each scanned column). It is a flat terrain autotile: a green grass strip on the left, a lighter teal shore edge, and dark teal water texture over the rest. There is no front-edge line, eave shadow, ellipse or vertical front face, so it is a flat ground tile and not a standing object. Under the terrain kind this is expected.

styleAnswer.evidence: At this scale the candidate reads as one dark teal block with a narrow lighter strip along its left edge. I can see only about 3 distinct lightness steps and no grass tufts, clumps or grain. The grass reference has layered greens with tuft clusters, and the paving reference has stones shaded one by one. The measured 9 tones per tile is higher than the references' 3 for grass and 7 for paving. But the picture shows much of that as near-identical shades, and 20% near-flat coverage against 0% for both references confirms large flat areas. Edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so the outline is not a black sticker line, and it is not the problem. The problem is the flat interior with little texture and shading depth next to the references. When in doubt, fail.
